title: ContractRecord
description: Contract and promotion terms — the grounding source for the RAG store described in BRD Section 5/13. The POC represents this as flat structured fields; the real RAG store will also need the underlying contract TEXT indexed for retrieval. This schema is the structured half of that — useful for deterministic checks (promo_end_date comparisons) even after the free-text RAG lookup is live, so keep both.

product_name.description: Human-readable product/bundle name, used directly in Stage 2's customer-facing explanation text.

base_mrc.description: Standard (non-promotional) recurring monthly charge for this product.

promo_name.description: Active or most-recent promotion name, null if none.

promo_end_date.description: When the promotion lapses (or lapsed). This is the single field that resolves the most common 'why did my bill go up' case (BRD's core motivating example) — STALENESS RISK: BRD §13 already flags this needs an automated weekly sync from the source contract system. Confirm ownership of that sync job in Sprint 1, not as a Sprint 3 afterthought.

min_term_months.description: Minimum contract commitment length, used for the PRODUCT_MINIMUM_COMMITMENT_LENGTH term type referenced elsewhere in the migration mapping work.

notes.description: Free-text contract notes (e.g. 'roaming billed separately, out-of-bundle'). In the POC this is a flat string used directly in Stage 2 reasoning; in production this is exactly the kind of text that should live in the vector-indexed RAG store rather than a fixed field, since real contract notes won't be this tidy.
